Partition label alignment, vertex marginals, consensus, and posterior modes

partition_mode_state.Rd

Label alignment, vertex marginal distributions, MAP consensus partitions, posterior uncertainty, and multimodal clustering of posterior partition ensembles using Peixoto's random label model (2021). These are the R counterparts of graph-tool's align_partition_labels(), partition_overlap(), PartitionModeState, and ModeClusterState.

Usage

align_partition_labels(x, y)
partition_overlap(x, y, norm = TRUE)
align_nested_partition_labels(x, y)
nested_partition_overlap(x, y, norm = TRUE)
partition_mode_state(partitions, relabel = TRUE, nested = NULL,
  converge = TRUE)
mode_marginals(mode, probability = FALSE, level = 0L)
mode_consensus(mode)
mode_uncertainty(mode, mle = TRUE)
mode_entropy(mode, mle = TRUE)
mode_lprob(mode, partition, mle = TRUE, align = FALSE)
mode_cluster_state(partitions, nested = NULL, b = NULL, relabel = TRUE,
  niter = 20L, converge = TRUE)
cluster_lprob(cluster, partition, mode = NULL, mle = TRUE, align = FALSE)
mode_summary(cluster)

Arguments

x, y

Flat integer label vectors (1-based) or nested lists of label vectors.

norm

Whether to return the normalized overlap in \([0, 1]\) or the raw number of matching nodes.

partitions

A list of flat or nested partitions, or the result object returned by sample_posterior.

relabel

Whether to align partition labels via maximum-weight bipartite matching when adding partitions.

nested

Logical indicating whether partitions are hierarchical, or NULL to infer from partitions.

converge

Whether to iterate label realignment until the random label model description length converges.

mode

A partition mode object returned by partition_mode_state() or stored inside mode_cluster_state()$modes. For mode_entropy(), a rgraphtool_mode_cluster object is also accepted. For cluster_lprob(), an optional 1-based mode index (or NULL for the full mode-mixture log-probability).

partition

A flat integer label vector or nested list of label vectors whose log-probability is evaluated under the mode or mode cluster.

align

If TRUE, align partition to the mode's consensus labels before evaluating the log-probability. Defaults to FALSE, matching graph-tool's posterior_lprob().

probability

If TRUE, return row-normalized marginal probabilities; otherwise return integer counts.

level

Hierarchy level (0-based) for nested modes.

mle

If TRUE, use maximum-likelihood marginal probabilities; if FALSE, use Dirichlet(1) posterior mean estimates.

b

Optional initial cluster assignment (1-based integer vector of length length(partitions)).

niter

Maximum number of split/sweep/merge optimization iterations. Set niter = 0 with b to score a fixed clustering.

cluster

A mode cluster object returned by mode_cluster_state().

Details

Pairwise label alignment solves the exact maximum-weight bipartite matching problem on the contingency matrix using the Hungarian algorithm. For ensembles, partition_mode_state() aligns all partitions to a common labelling by minimizing the integrated description length of the random label model, matching graph-tool 3.9's PartitionModeState entropy, posterior_entropy(), and posterior_cdev() numerically.

When the posterior distribution is multimodal, mode_cluster_state() clusters the sampled partitions into distinct modes by minimizing the mixture random label model description length, sorts the discovered modes by decreasing weight, and aligns secondary modes to the dominant mode.

Value

partition_mode_state() returns a rgraphtool_partition_mode list with M, B, entropy, posterior_entropy, posterior_cdev, marginals, consensus, and aligned partitions. mode_cluster_state() returns a rgraphtool_mode_cluster list with total entropy, clusters, number of modes K, effective number of modes Be, weights, and modes. mode_summary() formats the modes as a data frame.

References

Peixoto, T. P. (2021). Revealing consensus and dissensus between network partitions. Physical Review X 11, 021003. doi:10.1103/PhysRevX.11.021003

See also

sample_posterior, plot_marginals, demo("posterior_sampling"), demo("hierarchical_sampling")

Examples

bs <- list(c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2), c(2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1), c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3))
pm <- partition_mode_state(bs)
pm
#> <partition mode: M = 3, B = 3, uncertainty = 0.1111, DL = 17.8045 nats>
mode_marginals(pm, probability = TRUE)
#>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3]
#> [1,] 0.0000000 1.0000000 0.0000000
#> [2,] 0.0000000 1.0000000 0.0000000
#> [3,] 0.3333333 0.6666667 0.0000000
#> [4,] 1.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [5,] 1.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000
#> [6,] 0.6666667 0.0000000 0.3333333
mode_consensus(pm)
#> [1] 2 2 2 1 1 1
mode_uncertainty(pm)
#> [1] 0.1111111
